summary: Text for assistive technology only: screen readers read it, the screen does not show it. Use it to give a control or a symbol the words sighted users get from the layout.
whenToUse: A control whose visible content is not enough on its own, like a checkbox in a table row: "Select Button".
Extra context a sighted user gets from the layout, like " (opens in a new tab)" after an external link.
A label for a loading region while Skeleton placeholders are shown, like "Loading tokens".
whenNotToUse: Hiding content from everyone: use the hidden attribute or do not render it.
Naming an icon-only button: IconButton takes a label prop for that.
Long text or anything interactive: it is a span clipped to one pixel, so a link or button inside it would take focus while staying invisible.

dos.title: Add the words the layout implies
dos.text: Link with external does it for you: it adds a VisuallyHidden " (opens in a new tab)" after the label.

dos.title: Keep it short and specific
dos.text: Name the thing the control acts on: "Select Button" in a row, "Select all tokens" in the header.

donts.title: Repeat what is already visible
donts.text: If the visible label says it, screen readers read it twice.

donts.title: Use it to hide content you want to remove
donts.text: Screen reader users still hear it. Remove the content, or use the hidden attribute.

accessibility: Renders a span that stays in the accessibility tree: screen readers read its text in place.
Clipped to one pixel with clip-path and overflow hidden, positioned absolutely, so it takes no room in the layout.
white-space: nowrap keeps the words from being read one per line by some screen readers.
Accepts every native span attribute and spreads them, so an id for aria-describedby works.
contentGuidelines: Write it as part of the sentence it completes, with the leading space when it follows other text: " (opens in a new tab)".
Sentence case, no trailing period unless it is a full sentence.

anatomy.hidden: The clipped span, one pixel wide (border.width.1)
